newsitem.title: INDIA: India Reliance appoints global accountant.
newsitem.headline: India Reliance appoints global accountant.

text.p: India's largest private firm Reliance Industries Ltd on Monday said it appointed Deloitte, Touche, Tohmatsu International (DTTI) as its international accountant as a prelude to eventual listing of its securities in the United States.

"DTTI will assist us in adhering to international norms of financial reporting, accounting standards and disclosures in addition to those being followed now in accordance with the (Indian) Companies Act," a Reliance spokesman said.
"We will work closely with DTTI and auditors appointed under the Companies Act and thus be able to combine the best and relevant practices both Indian and international," he told Reuters.
"Indian auditors understand Indian taxes, legal and accounting systems better," the spokesman said.

He said the appointment is a prelude to quarterly reporting, consolidation of accounts, reconciliation and presentation of accounts according to generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) of the UK and the U.S.
Registration with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and eventual listing of Reliance's securities on overseas bourses are also on the anvil, the spokesman said.

International investors hold $1.5 billion of debt and equity in Reliance. Other international users of Reliance's financial reports would include rating agencies, global firms and potential international partners, he said.
He said the appointment would be good news for international investors, enabling them to compare Reliance with the rest of its international peer group.
Reliance, the first Indian firm to issue overseas equity, in the form of global depositary receipts (GDR) in 1992, has raised $914.0 million in foreign debt over the last 18 months.
It is the only Indian firm to be rated by three international rating agencies -- S & P, Moody's and NAIC.
